pairs.why: A's teal saucer is a bolder, more solid colored toy shape that fills the frame like the real cards, while B's pale silver disc is smaller and washed out.
B is a properly built, chunky side-view saucer with a full rounded body that reads as a solid toy object; A is a flat, thin, top-down disc.
B's helmet is built like a real object with soft, calm shading, closer to the real camera and vending machine, while A is an oddly constructed ball with a hard plastic sheen.
B has a believable helmet build and soft illustrated finish, whereas A is a featureless glossy white blob on a slick reflective ledge.
A's chunky, frame-filling telescope with warm wood legs matches the bold, solid shapes of the real binoculars and chair better than B's thinner, darker scope.
B has the painterly illustrated look, with a purple sky, readable moon terrain and soft light, while A looks like a plain, flat, dark 3D render.
B's warm, glowing, cartoon-solid dome with a lit door matches the cozy lit buildings in the real cards (lighthouse, motel) better than A's cool grey, slightly gritty scene.
The two are nearly identical in rendering, colour and build; B's dome is only marginally larger and smoother.
